```python
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.fea as fea
import pychrono.pardisomkl as mkl
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

print("Example: PyChrono using beam finite elements")
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Create the physical system
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
sys = chrono.ChSystemSMC()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create a mesh to contain FEA nodes & elements
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mesh = fea.ChMesh()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Create a beam section (shared by all Euler‐Bernoulli beams)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
msection = fea.ChBeamSectionEulerAdvanced()
beam_wy = 0.012
beam_wz = 0.025
msection.SetAsRectangularSection(beam_wy, beam_wz)
msection.SetYoungModulus(0.01e9)
msection.SetShearModulus(0.01e9 * 0.3)
msection.SetRayleighDamping(0.0)
msection.SetCentroid(0, 0.02)
msection.SetShearCenter(0, 0.1)
# rotate the section by 45 degrees (converted to radians):
msection.SetSectionRotation(45 * chrono.CH_DEG_TO_RAD)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Manually create three nodes and two elements in a row
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
beam_L = 0.1

hnode1 = fea.ChNodeFEAxyzrot()
hnode1.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0))
hnode1.SetRot(chrono.QUNIT)
mesh.AddNode(hnode1)

hnode2 = fea.ChNodeFEAxyzrot()
hnode2.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L, 0, 0))
hnode2.SetRot(chrono.QUNIT)
mesh.AddNode(hnode2)

hnode3 = fea.ChNodeFEAxyzrot()
hnode3.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L * 2, 0, 0))
hnode3.SetRot(chrono.QUNIT)
mesh.AddNode(hnode3)

# first beam element
be1 = fea.ChElementBeamEuler()
be1.SetNodes(hnode1, hnode2)
be1.SetSection(msection)
mesh.AddElement(be1)

# second beam element
be2 = fea.ChElementBeamEuler()
be2.SetNodes(hnode2, hnode3)
be2.SetSection(msection)
mesh.AddElement(be2)

# apply loads
hnode2.SetForce(chrono.ChVector3d(4, 2, 0))
hnode3.SetTorque(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -0.04, 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Fix hnode1 and hnode3 to ground via simple Boolean constraints
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# ground body
mtruss = chrono.ChBody()
mtruss.SetFixed(True)
sys.Add(mtruss)

# fix hnode3 completely
constr1 = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric()
constr1.Initialize(hnode3, mtruss, False,
                   hnode3.GetFrame(), mtruss.GetFrame())
constr1.SetConstrainedCoords(True, True, True,   # x,y,z
                             True, True, True)   # Rx,Ry,Rz
sys.Add(constr1)

# fix hnode1 in y,z translation only
constr2 = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric()
constr2.Initialize(hnode1, mtruss, False,
                   hnode1.GetFrame(), mtruss.GetFrame())
constr2.SetConstrainedCoords(False, True, True,   # x,y,z
                             False, False, False) # Rx,Ry,Rz
sys.Add(constr2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Use the ChBuilderBeamEuler shortcut to add a 5‐element beam
#    from (0,0,-0.1) to (0.2,0,-0.1), up=(0,1,0).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
builder = fea.ChBuilderBeamEuler()
builder.BuildBeam(mesh, msection, 5,
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, -0.1),
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0.2, 0, -0.1),
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0, 1, 0))

# fix the *end* of that beam and apply a load at its *start*  
last_beam_nodes = builder.GetLastBeamNodes()
last_beam_nodes[-1].SetFixed(True)
last_beam_nodes[0].SetForce(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -1, 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) *** NEW *** add another beam segment ***
#    start at the last node above, end at (0.2,0.1,-0.1), up=(0,1,0)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# grab the same last node as the 'A' point:
A_node = last_beam_nodes[-1]
builder.BuildBeam(mesh, msection, 5,
                  A_node,
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0.2, 0.1, -0.1),
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0, 1, 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8) Finalize FEA mesh setup
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mesh.SetAutomaticGravity(False)
sys.Add(mesh)

# add a beam‐shape visualization
vis_shape = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
vis_shape.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_ELEM_BEAM_MZ)
vis_shape.SetColorscaleMinMax(-0.4, 0.4)
vis_shape.SetSmoothFaces(True)
vis_shape.SetWireframe(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(vis_shape)

# add node coordinate‐systems glyphs
node_csys = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
node_csys.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_CSYS)
node_csys.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)
node_csys.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)
node_csys.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)
node_csys.SetZbufferHide(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(node_csys)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9) Irrlicht 3D viewer
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('FEA beams')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0.1, 0.1, 0.2))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# switch to a Pardiso MKL solver for better FEA accuracy
msolver = mkl.ChSolverPardisoMKL()
sys.SetSolver(msolver)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10) Run the simulation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
tstep = 1e-3
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(tstep)
```

Below is a self‐contained Python script that uses PyChrono to build a small cantilever beam out of Euler‐Bernoulli beam finite elements, visualizes it with Irrlicht, applies gravity, fixes the root node, and runs a real‐time simulation loop. You can copy & paste this into a file (e.g. `beam_demo.py`) and run it with `python3 beam_demo.py` (make sure PyChrono with the FEA and Irrlicht modules is installed).

```python
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.fea as fea
import pychrono.irrlicht as irr

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Initialize the Chrono system
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
system.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, -9.81, 0))   # gravity

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create an FEA mesh and define beam section & material properties
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mesh = fea.ChMesh()

# Define a circular beam section (Euler beam)
section = chrono.ChBeamSectionEuler()
E = 2e11                # Young's modulus [Pa]
rho = 7800              # density [kg/m^3]
nu = 0.3                # Poisson ratio (for G)
section.SetYoungModulus(E)
section.SetGwithPoissonRatio(E / (2*(1+nu)), nu)
section.SetDensity(rho)
section.SetAsCircularSection(0.02)  # radius = 0.02 m

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Create nodes along the X axis and add them to the mesh
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
num_elems   = 6
elem_length = 0.5
nodes = []

for i in range(num_elems + 1):
    x = i * elem_length
    node = fea.ChNodeFEAxyz(chrono.ChVectorD(x, 0, 0))
    node.SetMass(0)           # lumped mass = 0 (mass comes from section)
    mesh.AddNode(node)
    nodes.append(node)

# Fix the first node (cantilever root)
nodes[0].SetFixed(True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Create beam elements connecting the nodes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
for i in range(num_elems):
    beam = fea.ChElementBeamEuler()
    beam.SetNodes(nodes[i], nodes[i+1])    # assign start/end nodes
    beam.SetSection(section)               # assign section & material
    mesh.AddElement(beam)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Add the mesh to the system
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
system.Add(mesh)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Create visualization assets for the mesh
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This will draw each beam element in wireframe with a default color
vis_mesh = fea.ChVisualizationFEAmesh(mesh)
vis_mesh.SetWireframe(True)
vis_mesh.SetDefaultMeshColor(chrono.ChColor(0.2, 0.5, 0.8))
mesh.AddAsset(vis_mesh)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Create the Irrlicht application for real‐time rendering
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
application = irr.ChIrrApp(system, "PyChrono Beam FEA Demo", irr.dimension2du(1024, 768))
application.AddTypicalSky()
application.AddTypicalLogo()
application.AddTypicalLights()
application.AddTypicalCamera(irr.vector3df(3,1.5,3))

# Bind and update all assets (must be done before simulation)
application.AssetBindAll()
application.AssetUpdateAll()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8) Simulation loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
application.SetTimestep(1e-3)
while application.GetDevice().run():
    application.BeginScene()
    application.DrawAll()
    application.DoStep()
    application.EndScene()
```

Explanation of the key steps:

1. **System initialization**  
   We create a `ChSystemNSC` and enable gravity.

2. **FEA Mesh and Beam Section**  
   A `ChMesh` holds our FEA nodes and elements. We define an Euler‐beam section (`ChBeamSectionEuler`) with Young’s modulus, density, Poisson ratio and a circular cross‐section radius.

3. **Nodes**  
   We build a straight line of nodes along the X axis, spaced by `elem_length`. The first node is fixed to simulate a cantilever.

4. **Beam Elements**  
   We instantiate a `ChElementBeamEuler` for each pair of adjacent nodes, assign the beam section, and add them to the mesh.

5. **Visualization**  
   We attach a `ChVisualizationFEAmesh` asset to the mesh so that the beam elements are drawn in wireframe with a chosen color.

6. **Irrlicht Application**  
   We set up a `ChIrrApp`, add lights, sky, camera, bind all assets and enter the real‐time loop. Each loop we render the scene and advance the Chrono solver by one timestep.

import pychrono as chrono            # main PyChrono module
import pychrono.fea as fea           # finite elements
import pychrono.pardisomkl as mkl    # Pardiso MKL solver
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr  # Irrlicht visualizer

print("Example: PyChrono Euler–Bernoulli beam using ChBuilderBeamEuler")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Create the physical system
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
sys = chrono.ChSystemSMC()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Create a mesh container (will hold beam elements and nodes)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mesh = fea.ChMesh()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Define an Euler–Bernoulli beam section
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
beam_wy = 0.012
beam_wz = 0.025
msection = fea.ChBeamSectionEulerAdvanced()
msection.SetAsRectangularSection(beam_wy, beam_wz)
msection.SetYoungModulus(0.01e9)          
msection.SetShearModulus(0.01e9 * 0.3)    
msection.SetRayleighDamping(0.000)        
msection.SetCentroid(0, 0.02)             
msection.SetShearCenter(0, 0.1)           
msection.SetSectionRotation(45 * chrono.CH_RAD_TO_DEG)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Build a single Euler–Bernoulli beam from A to B with 5 elements
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
builder = fea.ChBuilderBeamEuler()

ptA = chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, -0.1)
ptB = chrono.ChVectorD(0.2, 0, -0.1)
up  = chrono.ChVectorD(0, 1, 0)

# BuildBeam(mesh, section, nsegments, start, end, fix_start, fix_end, up_dir)
builder.BuildBeam(mesh, msection,
                  5,
                  ptA, ptB,
                  True, True,
                  up)

# Extract the first and last nodes from the builder
first_nodes = builder.GetFirstBeamNodes()   # Python list of start‐end nodes
last_nodes  = builder.GetLastBeamNodes()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Replace direct SetFixed on the first node with a constraint
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# first_nodes[0].SetFixed(True)    # <-- commented out per instruction

# Instead, create a fixed generic mate linking first node to a fixed truss
mtruss = chrono.ChBody()
mtruss.SetFixed(True)
sys.Add(mtruss)

constr_first = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric()
constr_first.Initialize(first_nodes[0], mtruss,
                        False,
                        first_nodes[0].Frame(), first_nodes[0].Frame())
constr_first.SetConstrainedCoords(True, True, True,  # x,y,z translations
                                  True, True, True)  # Rx,Ry,Rz rotations
sys.Add(constr_first)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Fix the last node directly (per instruction #3)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back().SetFixed(True)  # C++ style
last_nodes[-1].SetFixed(True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Apply a force of (0, -1, 0) to the first node
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
first_nodes[0].SetForce(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -1, 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8) Disable automatic gravity for the FEA mesh and add it to the system
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mesh.SetAutomaticGravity(False)
sys.Add(mesh)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9) FEA visualization (unchanged)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

vis_beam_mz.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_ELEM_BEAM_MZ)
vis_beam_mz.SetColorscaleMinMax(-0.4, 0.4)
vis_beam_mz.SetSmoothFaces(True)
vis_beam_mz.SetWireframe(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(vis_beam_mz)

vis_nodes = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
vis_nodes.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_CSYS)
vis_nodes.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)
vis_nodes.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)
vis_nodes.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)
vis_nodes.SetZbufferHide(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(vis_nodes)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10) Setup Irrlicht visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Euler–Bernoulli Beam Example')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0.1, 0.1, 0.2))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11) Use MKL Pardiso solver
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
msolver = mkl.ChSolverPardisoMKL()
sys.SetSolver(msolver)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12) Simulation loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
t_step = 1e-3
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(t_step)
